clue.text: Individual tango lesson's included

indicators.note: something included is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the lesson a fable teaches is its moral; the 's is read as 'is'
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance student booking a one-to-one tango class.
explanation.walkthrough: The tango letter sits inside the lesson word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human being, an individual person as opposed to a god.

clue.text: First sign of table manners, sitting higher, being demure

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter
in a down entry, sitting higher means placed above, so the manners piece comes first

blocks.note: modes are ways or manners of doing things
the opening letter of table

explanation.surface: Good table manners shown by a well-bred diner sitting up straight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the manners word sits above the table's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and demure both describe someone reserved and unassuming in behaviour.

clue.text: Running flush with free change of cards?

indicators.note: running colours spread and mix, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A poker player on a flush asking for a free swap of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a reshuffle literally mixes cards, though the word usually means a change of government ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reshuffle literally rearranges a pack of cards, and figuratively changes the line-up of a cabinet.

clue.text: A writer's inspiration: soldiers set upon sailor, rascal going to Spain for seaside fun

indicators.note: in a down entry, set upon means placed on top of what follows
going to joins the rascal to the next piece, placed straight after it

blocks.note: taken as written
a muse is a source of creative inspiration
ordinary soldiers are the men
tar is old slang for a sailor
a cad is a dishonourable man
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A writer's story idea: troops attack a seaman while a scoundrel flees to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A seaside amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and games found on British seafronts.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade, full of slot machines and games, is a staple entertainment of British seaside resorts.

clue.text: A selection from delicatessens I blended to be practical

indicators.note: a selection is a run of letters picked out of the following words as they stand

blocks.note: the run starts inside the shop name and finishes inside the last word

explanation.surface: A mixed sample from the deli counter turns out to be a sensible choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible and practical are near synonyms for down-to-earth, reasonable choices.

clue.text: Love is painful when it's over

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: The heartache that comes after a relationship ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's over' sounds like a break-up but signals turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the name is used for sexual love itself.

clue.text: My inside-out coat would be funny in this

definitions.text: My inside-out coat would be funny in this

indicators.note: something funny is odd or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: every letter of these words

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a coat inside out would get laughs in a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a garment worn wrong way out is a classic sitcom gag. 'inside-out' looks like an instruction but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy, or sitcom, is a TV comedy built on everyday mishaps like wearing clothes the wrong way out.

clue.text: Roar subdued by black bear

indicators.note: in a down entry, subdued by means kept beneath, so the black piece sits on top

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to rave is to shout wildly

explanation.surface: A black bear's roar is silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is a verb here, to endure, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to face or endure it, which is one sense of the verb bear.

clue.text: Service all the same, banged down the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central pair of letters, the rest discarded
in a down entry, down places the second piece below the first

blocks.note: even so means nevertheless
the two central letters of banged

explanation.surface: A church service where all the same hymns were belted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banged down' sounds like slamming something, but 'down' places the middle letters below.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is a church service.

clue.text: One's sent flying by a competitor

definitions.text: One's sent flying by a competitor

blocks.clueFragment: One's sent flying by a competitor
blocks.note: surface reading: someone is knocked over by a rival in a race or match
setter's reading: an object is thrown through the air by a field athlete

explanation.surface: A runner is barged over by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent flying' suggests a collision, but here it is a throw in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy disc hurled in a field event travels through the air after an athlete spins and releases it.

clue.text: This inferior crew will lose face in the East End

blocks.note: the famous annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge, where the weaker crew loses
in Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in London's East End, this contest's name stands for a person's face

explanation.surface: A weak team is going to be humiliated in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thames rowing race between Oxford and Cambridge is the event; Cockney rhyming slang, from London's East End, uses its name to mean 'face'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slower of two university crews loses the rowing race, and the race's name is rhyming slang for the face.

clue.text: Tired of circle that's taken over squat

indicators.note: something taken over is turned upside down, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

blocks.note: a dial is a round face, as on a clock
squat means short and low to the ground

explanation.surface: Someone worn out by a circle of squat exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squat' looks like the exercise, but it is the adjective, short and low.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid low means brought down by illness or exhaustion, so feeling drained and tired.

clue.text: Prepared canapes with posh filling in this?

definitions.text: Prepared canapes with posh filling in this?

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked up from its raw ingredients, so the letters are rearranged
a filling goes inside something, so the posh letter is put within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: Fancy party nibbles with a smart stuffing might be cooked in this pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a pan you might cook canapes in. U for upper-class comes from the old U and non-U distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a kitchen pot in which food might be prepared, so the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: Documents journalists' output

blocks.note: first meaning: official sheets such as identity documents
second meaning: newspapers, what reporters produce

explanation.surface: Records produced by reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both personal documents (show your papers) and newspapers, the daily work of the press.

clue.text: Cavalier turned to get round of applause

blocks.note: milk that has turned has gone off
give them a big hand means applaud them

explanation.surface: A Royalist cavalier turned round to receive applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' suggests a Civil War Royalist soldier, but it is an adjective meaning dismissive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a casual, careless attitude that shows little concern for others.

clue.text: Where shepherds watched their flock by night, as far as one can see

definitions.text: Where shepherds watched their flock by night
as far as one can see

blocks.clueFragment: Where shepherds watched their flock by night
blocks.note: first meaning, playful: the pasture where the Nativity shepherds saw the angels, a field of a vision

blocks.clueFragment: as far as one can see
blocks.note: second meaning: the whole area visible to the eye

explanation.surface: The carol line about the shepherds is set beside the extent of one's sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half quotes the Christmas carol; the shepherds were in a field when the angel's vision came to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means the full extent seen by the eye, and also jokingly names the field where the angelic appearance happened.

clue.text: Maybe cricket nets beginning to produce gold for test specialist

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
a net catches and holds something, so the next letter goes inside
for here means in addition to, putting the gold piece after the rest

blocks.note: a cricket is an example of an insect, hence 'maybe'
first letter of produce
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Cricket practice nets begin producing gold for a Test match specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket', 'nets' and 'test' all suggest the sport; the cricket is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector examines and tests things for compliance, such as a quality or exam examiner.

clue.text: Fools rushed to leave Portugal and checked out

indicators.note: the Portugal letter has to leave, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: an ass is a foolish person
sped means hurried
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Foolish holidaymakers hurried out of Portugal and left their hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked out' reads like leaving a hotel but means examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To check out something is to examine or evaluate it, the same as assess.

clue.text: Dearest darling, say dinner's ending with love, love!

blocks.note: the sweet is the dessert course that ends a meal
love is zero in tennis scoring, so two loves are a pair of zeros

explanation.surface: A romantic toast at the end of a dinner date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: endearments like 'dearest' and 'darling'. 'Dinner's ending' is the pudding course, not the last letter of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmured endearments such as dearest and darling are the classic examples of affectionate, empty words between lovers.

clue.text: One can't see a thing when it's fully visible

definitions.text: One can't see a thing when it's fully visible

blocks.clueFragment: One can't see a thing when it's fully visible
blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox about something being in plain view yet unseen
setter's reading: the skin flap over the eye shows completely only when it is shut, blocking sight

explanation.surface: A riddle: something in plain sight that leaves you seeing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The part is fully on show only when the eye is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin covering the eye is only completely visible when lowered, and then its owner sees nothing.

clue.text: Complete depression, dreadful daughter won't open up repeatedly

indicators.note: the daughter abbreviation refuses to start the words, and 'repeatedly' applies that to both pieces

blocks.note: a dent is a hollow pressed into a surface
dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A total low mood that keeps the daughter from opening up.
explanation.walkthrough: D for daughter is the first letter of each piece, and both lose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and complete are synonyms meaning whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Go to crush street meeting

indicators.note: crushing presses one thing hard against the next, so the two pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: a go is an attempt, a try
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Arranging to see one's crush on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' suggests a romantic interest, which fits the definition, but here it presses the two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting, especially one arranged between lovers.

clue.text: Foul! Deflected volley — French one ahead

indicators.note: a deflected ball changes course, so these letters are knocked into a new order
ahead puts the French piece in front of the rest

blocks.note: un is French for one
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee's cry at a deflected tennis volley from a French player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul!' sounds like a sports shout, but it is an adjective meaning ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlovely means unpleasant or ugly, which is the adjective sense of foul.

clue.text: One's full of hot desire

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so the hot letter is placed within

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards; the 's reads as 'is'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone burning with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long for it, so the word works as a noun or verb of yearning.

clue.text: Quite salty ultimately, bottle offering Oriental taste

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: so means very or quite, as in 'so good'
the last letter of salty
bottle and sauce both mean cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A bottle with a rather salty flavour from East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container for the condiment, but it means nerve, and so does sauce in the sense of impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Soy sauce is the salty condiment of Chinese and Japanese cooking, a characteristic East Asian flavour.

clue.text: I'll net wriggling thing for soup

indicators.note: something wriggling twists about, so the letters squirm into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone promising to catch a squirming creature for the cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wriggling thing' reads as an eel or worm, but 'wriggling' is the signal and 'thing for soup' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are pulses commonly cooked into soup, so one is an ingredient for it.

clue.text: I'm reflecting, suppressed, taking time with repeated hesitations

definitions.note: the clue speaks in the first person: the speaker is the answer

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the next word is read backwards
taking means holding something within, so the time letter goes inside

blocks.note: to suppress something is to hide it
T is the abbreviation for time
er is the sound of hesitating, given twice

explanation.surface: Someone thinking things over, holding back and slowly umming and erring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' is the definition: the speaker who reflects, holds back and keeps saying 'er' is one who cannot decide.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditherer is a person who hesitates and cannot make up their mind, which is what the speaker describes being.

clue.text: Not fully roadworthy bridge crossing two things

definitions.note: a hybrid is the cross between two things

indicators.note: neither word is used in full, so the run is taken from parts of the two

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A road bridge in poor repair spanning two features.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring or product of crossing two different varieties or kinds.
